clearedSpotChecks.check: Which PoolManager shift, SIGNEXTEND and BYTE sites reach the non-literal arms of Monad's emitter (varsites.py over build/PoolManager.json minus the 1,205 literal sites of cycle 28 sitearms.json).
clearedSpotChecks.note: I reran scripts/varsites.py into my scratch directory and got the same totals (SHR 99, SHL 46, SAR 19, SIGNEXTEND 114, BYTE 3) and the same 22 shift sites plus one BYTE at pc 24006; the output equals out/varsites.json. The split is consistent with sitearms.py: a site with a literal count takes shift_by_literal, a literal value with a run-time count takes shift_literal_by_non_literal, so the remaining sites are the ones that reach shift_*_by_non_literal. The sentence that BYTE with a run-time index is not reached is too broad. sitearms.json lists two BYTE sites with a literal table and a run-time index, pc 21416 and 23652, from src/libraries/BitMath.sol:45 and :22. What is true is that no BYTE site has both operands non-literal. Those two sites take the literal-value arm, which cycle 29 already cleared for chain 143 (Emitter::byte() 0x37f1f0 with the two PoolManager tables), so the wording changes nothing about coverage. The sites in src are the ones the item names: TickMath.sol:141-213 r := shr(f, r) with f = shr(128, r), BitMath.sol:15-19 shr(r, x), and Slot0.sol:73 setTick.

clearedSpotChecks.check: shift_general_reg_by_non_literal<SHL, SHR, SAR> of monad 0.16.7 (gcc 15.2.0) run from the package text in the x86 model with the register allocator, spill and release paths lifted (shiftvar), and the AVX and stack-offset paths through Emitter::shl, shr and sar (shiftfull).
clearedSpotChecks.note: I copied the scripts to my scratch directory, pointed them at the same objdump text (out/fn), and changed the seeds to 9130 and 9131. shiftvar: 3000 cases, 180000 runs, 0 mismatches, 0 clobbers, 0 bookkeeping faults. shiftfull: 2996 cases, 149800 runs, 0 mismatches, 0 clobbers. Four states stopped at the emitter's own assertion at virtual_stack.cpp:526, which is the same limit of generated states the item reports. Planted faults still fail under my seeds: shr-avx-dword-bound gave 893 wrong-result runs in 399 cases, and spill-store-missing gave 200 clobbers in 400 cases. A read-only eth_call on https://rpc.monad.xyz (web3_clientVersion Monad/0.16.7, block 0x77f27f0) of init code computing shr(256, 2^256-1), shl(255, 1), sar(256, -1), shr(1, 2^256-1) and shl(2^32+1, 1) returned 0, 2^255, 2^256-1, 2^255-1 and 0, as the specification requires. That call shows the RPC path; it does not show which engine ran it. The provenance of the out/fn text as the gcc build of monad 0.16.7 comes from cycle 29 and I did not refetch the package.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Emitter::write_to_final_stack_offsets 0x3816e0, the block-exit routine, run in the model on random block-exit states (wfso.py).
clearedSpotChecks.note: I reran wfso.py with seed 9133: 1500 cases, 30000 runs, 0 bad final offsets. Removing the store emission at 0x381b0d gave 1470 bad runs out of 1500, so the check can fail. This routine decides the word each EVM stack slot holds at every block exit, including the exits of Pool.swap blocks at src/libraries/Pool.sol:344. A fault there would reach every library, so a wrong clearance here would cost the most. Under generated states it holds. The open part is the lead the item already filed at medium priority: real block-entry states and whole-block streams for FullMath, SqrtPriceMath, SwapMath and Pool.swap were not compared against the clang listing. I agree that lead should stay open.
